learn.title: Storage services, tiers, redundancy, moving files and migration
objectives: Compare Azure Blob Storage, Azure Files, Queue Storage, Table Storage and managed disks, and pick the right one for a workload.
Describe the Hot, Cool, Cold and Archive access tiers and their trade-offs.
Describe the redundancy options: LRS, ZRS, GRS, GZRS, RA-GRS and RA-GZRS.
Choose a tool for moving files: AzCopy, Azure Storage Explorer or Azure File Sync.
Describe migration with Azure Migrate and offline transfer with Azure Data Box.
concepts: Blob Storage
Object storage for massive amounts of unstructured data such as images, video, backups and logs, reached over HTTP/HTTPS.
Azure Files
Fully managed file shares reached over SMB or NFS, which can be mounted at the same time by cloud and on-premises machines.
Queue Storage
Stores large numbers of messages so that application components can communicate asynchronously.
Table Storage
A NoSQL key/attribute store for structured, schemaless data.
Managed disks
Block-level storage volumes for Azure VMs, managed by Azure.
Access tiers
Hot (frequent access), Cool (at least 30 days), Cold (at least 90 days) and Archive (at least 180 days, offline). Cooler tiers cost less to store but more to access.
Rehydration
Moving an archived blob to an online tier before it can be read. It can take hours.
Redundancy

Azure Storage always keeps multiple copies. LRS: three copies in one datacenter. ZRS: three availability zones. GRS and GZRS: an extra copy in a secondary region. RA- versions allow reads from the secondary.
AzCopy and Storage Explorer
AzCopy is a command-line tool for copying data. Storage Explorer is a graphical app that uses AzCopy behind the scenes.
Azure Migrate and Data Box
Azure Migrate is a hub for discovering, assessing and migrating workloads. Data Box is a rugged device for offline transfer of large data sets (about 80 TB usable).
comparisons: Blob: objects over HTTP, for apps and unstructured data. Files: shared folders over SMB or NFS, for lift-and-shift file shares.
LRS protects against drive and rack failure, ZRS against a zone outage, GRS against a regional outage.
Both copy data to a secondary region. Only RA-GRS lets you read the secondary without a failover.
AzCopy vs Storage Explorer vs File Sync
AzCopy: scripted copies. Storage Explorer: point-and-click management. File Sync: ongoing sync and caching of Azure Files on Windows Server.
Use the network when bandwidth allows. Use Data Box when the data is huge or the connection is slow, costly or unavailable.
traps: Archive blobs can't be read straight away; they must be rehydrated first.
Archive can be set only on individual blobs, not as an account's default tier.
Moving a blob out of Cool, Cold or Archive early can incur an early-deletion charge.
GRS does not let you read the secondary region unless you choose RA-GRS or RA-GZRS (or a failover happens).
AzCopy sync is one-way; Azure File Sync keeps file shares in sync continuously.
Data Box moves data offline; it isn't a network connection.
revision: Unstructured objects: Blob. SMB/NFS shares: Files. Messages: Queue. NoSQL entities: Table. VM volumes: Disks.
Hot, then Cool (30 days), Cold (90 days), Archive (180 days, offline).
LRS: one datacenter. ZRS: three zones. GRS: two regions. GZRS: zones plus a second region.
RA- = read access to the secondary region.
AzCopy = CLI, Storage Explorer = GUI, File Sync = cache Azure Files on Windows Server.
Azure Migrate = discover, assess, migrate. Data Box = ship the data on a device.

2. Managed disks are designed to be used with virtual machines.
3. Queue Storage helps decouple parts of an application.

opts: Data must be rehydrated before each read, adding delay and retrieval cost

questions.q: Which Azure Storage service provides fully managed cloud file shares?

questions.q: What does locally redundant storage (LRS) do?
opts: Copies data to a secondary region
Keeps three copies of data within a single datacenter in the primary region
Keeps one copy only, with no redundancy
Keeps copies in three availability zones

questions.q: A company wants its storage data to survive the loss of an availability zone, but every copy must stay in the primary region. Which redundancy option fits?
What does geo-redundant storage (GRS) add compared with LRS?
opts: Read access to data from any region
Copies in three availability zones of the same region
An asynchronous copy of the data in a secondary region

questions.q: Which redundancy option is the lowest-cost option?
What does the 'RA' in RA-GRS stand for?
A company wants its data to stay available if one datacenter in its region suffers a power failure, but data must not leave the region. Which redundancy option fits best?
questions.e: ZRS spreads copies across zones in one region, so a datacenter failure doesn't cause an outage, and data stays in that region.

questions.q: Which redundancy options protect data against the loss of an entire Azure region?
Which redundancy option combines zone redundancy in the primary region with an asynchronous copy in a secondary region?
Is this statement true or false? 'With GRS, applications can read from the secondary region at any time.'
opts: False. GRS doesn't copy data to another region
True. GRS always allows reads from both regions
False. With GRS the secondary isn't readable unless a failover occurs; RA-GRS adds read access

questions.q: What does geo-zone-redundant storage (GZRS) combine?
opts: ZRS in the primary region plus an asynchronous copy to a secondary region
Two copies on a single disk
LRS in two zones and nothing else

questions.q: How is data copied from the primary region to the secondary region with GRS?
opts: Synchronously, so the secondary is always identical in real time
Asynchronously, so the secondary may lag slightly behind the primary

questions.q: With GRS, data is copied to the secondary region asynchronously. What does this mean if the primary region fails?
opts: No data can ever be lost
Recent writes that hadn't replicated yet may be lost after failover
The secondary region always receives writes before the primary

questions.q: A team stores test data that can be easily recreated. They want the lowest storage cost and don't need regional or zone protection. Which redundancy option fits?
Critical data must survive a zone outage and a regional outage, and must be readable from the secondary region at all times. Which option fits?

Evaluate these statements.
1. LRS protects against the failure of a single drive or rack.
2. ZRS stores copies in a secondary region.
3. GZRS protects against both zone and regional outages.
Which statements are true?
Data is stored with LRS. A disaster affects the whole datacenter. What's the risk?
opts: All copies could be lost or unavailable, because LRS keeps them in one datacenter
No risk, because LRS uses three zones
Only the Archive tier is affected
No risk, because LRS copies data to another region

questions.q: Regulations require that data never leaves a specific region, but the company still wants protection against a datacenter failure. Which option meets both needs?
Is this statement true or false? 'Azure Storage always keeps multiple copies of your data, whichever redundancy option you choose.'
opts: False. Copies are kept only if you buy a backup service
False. Only GRS keeps more than one copy
True, but only for Queue Storage
